title: United Airlines Flights Resume After ‘Widespread System Outage’
summary: The brief disruption, after a nationwide ground stop last week, added to concerns about air travel ahead of a busy Thanksgiving travel period.

A “widespread system outage” grounded United flights on Monday afternoon before it was resolved after about an hour, unnerving travelers as the nation’s aviation system was recovering from the ground stoppage that paralyzed air traffic late last week.


The airline said that “while some flights were delayed, there was no impact on flights in progress, or on United Express flights,” referring to its regional network of smaller carriers that operate shorter flights on United’s behalf. Some passengers reported delays that carried over into the evening hours as the airline worked to get its delayed flights airborne.


In an earlier statement announcing the disruption, which was reported just before 5 p.m. Eastern time, United said that it was “troubleshooting a technology issue affecting departing flights” but that there was “no impact on flights in progress.”


United did not provide additional details about the outage, which was reported just days before millions of Americans, many of them jittery about delays and other problems with air travel, are expected to fly for the Thanksgiving holiday.


People have been rattled by a series of technical outages that have disrupted their daily lives. Last week, many Microsoft systems went down, bringing email, work messaging platforms and other corporate systems to a halt. Then there was the five-hour national halt to all flights caused by a seemingly minor upgrade to the communications system used by air traffic controllers. And on Monday, JPMorgan Chase said a “[software bug](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/16/us/bank-outages-down.html) ” had impeded its ability to process some financial transactions.


Among the passengers who were delayed by the United outage on Monday was David Goss, 67, of Chicago, who said his United flight was grounded in Mexico City for about an hour before departing for Chicago on Monday evening.
